primary_claim: GPT-OSS-20B's navigation behaviour in 2D grid-world tasks is broadly consistent with its own internally decoded 'cognitive map' of the environment (83% action accuracy relative to the true-grid optimal policy), and a large share of its apparent failures (58%, up to 88% in low-density/small grids) are actually optimal moves given its inaccurate internal beliefs, suggesting many errors reflect limited capability rather than a lack of goal-directedness.

effect.metric: action accuracy vs. optimal policy on true grid, and on agent's decoded cognitive map
effect.value: 83% action accuracy overall consistency with internal world model; 58% (up to 88% for low-density/small-medium grids) of true-grid mistakes are optimal under the agent's decoded cognitive map

stated_future_work: Extending to more realistic settings, where the gap between behavioural and representational evaluation may be even more consequential
Establishing causal links between environment and plan representations and the agent's behaviour, e.g. via causal mediation techniques
Testing across architectures and scales to ensure generality of findings
limitations_stated: The controlled grid-world setup is intentionally simple and may not transfer to complex real-world environments

Preliminary partial-observability attempts with GPT-5.1-Thinking showed pathological behaviours (redundant backtracking, moving into dead-ends), making it hard to separate capability failures from goal-directedness failures
quote: the agent's behaviour is broadly consistent with its internal world model (83% action accuracy across conditions)
